title: Sunset legacy longpoll endpoints and migration SDK assist playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
We will sunset the legacy longpoll/polling endpoints ("/v0/longpoll" and the compatibility polling shim used by older SDKs) that were originally introduced as a lower-latency fallback for clients that could not support streaming sockets. This ticket defines the migration requirements, SDK assist tooling, acceptance criteria, rollout timeline, and communication plan for customers and partners.

Background and motivation:
- Longpoll endpoints were added in 2022 to support clients behind restrictive networking but predate our unified streaming and reconnect semantics.
- Ongoing maintenance of the compat shim increases operational complexity and causes inconsistencies with new routing/fallback behavior within the runtime.
- Unified streaming (WebSocket/HTTP2) and the new reconnect API (introduced in api-2025.11) provide equivalent or superior guarantees for latency and resilience.

Goals:
- Provide a clear migration path for customers using longpoll endpoints or legacy SDKs that rely on the compat shim.
- Build SDK helpers and a migration-check tool to detect longpoll usage and offer a one-click migration guide.
- Coordinate a staged sunset with monitoring and rollback thresholds to limit customer disruption.

Non-goals:
- We will not change server-side streaming semantics or introduce new streaming protocols in this effort.
- We will not auto-migrate customer traffic without explicit opt-in.

Scope and affected surface area:
- Endpoints: /v0/longpoll, /v0/poll-compat, legacy query params to /generate that trigger polling mode.
- SDKs: python-sdk versions < 1.9.0, js-sdk versions < 2.4.3 (we will publish shim-detection for other languages).
- Console: Add per-project deprecation warnings in the Routes & Endpoints page.
- Docs: Update API reference and Quickstarts.

Planned mitigation and migration approach:
1) Detect & notify (April 2026): deploy passive telemetry that emits an admin-visible list of projects making longpoll requests. Provide in-console banners for affected projects with a migration checklist.
2) SDK Assist (April–May 2026): ship python/js SDK updates with:
   - automatic reconnect wrapper that implements equivalent backoff and resume semantics over WebSocket/HTTP2,
   - a runtime flag that preserves prior client semantics during canary testing,
   - a migration-check tool (CLI) that scans code for longpoll usage patterns and produces a migration report.
3) Documentation & examples (April 2026): a migration playbook with code diffs, sample PRs, and Confluence step-by-step guides.
4) Canary & phased shutdown (May–June 2026): a 4-week canary per-region, followed by 2-week global read-only mode, then full shutdown.

Progress updates and decisions so far:
- 2026-03-05: PM/Eng sync — decision to not backport streaming to older SDK versions; instead provide a compatibility wrapper in newer SDK releases.
- 2026-03-09: Design review — agreed on in-console banner language (see design mock in Confluence link).
- 2026-03-12: Eng implementation plan approved; ENG-21087 will implement telemetry and console banner hooks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Auto-migration vs assisted-migration: auto-migration reduces support load but risks breaking older integrations. We chose assisted with tooling to minimize breakage.
- Keeping longpoll as fallthrough vs shutdown: maintaining both increases code surface and testing burden; sunset favors long-term reliability.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- A1: Passive telemetry identifies >= 95% of active longpoll clients and surfaces them in the project console.
- A2: SDK releases (python 1.9.x, js 2.4.x) include migration helpers and preserve existing semantics behind a feature flag.
- A3: Migration CLI reports actionable changes for 90% of scanned repos in internal dogfood.
- A4: Documentation and code examples published and linked from console banners.
- A5: During canary, error rate for migrated clients stays within +1.5 SLO of baseline and customer support escalations do not exceed threshold.

Monitoring & KPIs:
- Telemetry coverage: % projects with detected longpoll traffic (dashboard).
- Migration uptake: % affected projects that opt into the SDK wrapper or migrate to streaming within 8 weeks.
- Runtime errors: 5xx rate and client reconnect latencies for migrated traffic.
- Support volume: number of tickets tagged "longpoll-migration" per week.

Rollout timeline (proposed):
- April 6–20, 2026: Passive telemetry and console banners (ENG-21087).
- April 20–May 10, 2026: SDK assist releases (python 1.9.0, js 2.4.3) + migration CLI beta (ENG-21405).
- May 11–June 7, 2026: Per-region canaries (start with us-west1, eu-west1).
- June 8–June 21, 2026: Global read-only mode for longpoll endpoints with continued banner + migration windows.
- June 22, 2026: Planned full shutdown of longpoll endpoints (subject to rollback conditions).

Rollback & contingency plan:
- If error rate or critical customer impact exceeds thresholds during canary, pause rollout and revert the canary region to full compat layer for affected projects.
- Support playbook to escalate impacted customers and provide temporary IP allow-listing or temporary legacy flag for specific projects.

Communication plan:
- In-console banner + project admin email (2-week notice before canary).
- Developer newsletter article with migration guide.
- Dedicated support page and migration Slack channel (#longpoll-migration).
- Templates for customer success outreach (high-impact customers).

Open decisions / blockers:
- Whether to allow a permanent "legacy-mode" account opt-in for regulated customers who cannot migrate before June 22. (Action: PM to propose policy by 2026-03-25).
- Backwards compatibility for third-party proxies that rely on polling semantics. (Action: Eng to prototype proxy detection by 2026-04-01).

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence migration playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/LP-migration-playbook (draft)
- Design mock for console banners: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/console-banners-mock
- SDK PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/4120, https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/7291
- Telemetry dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.io/d/longpoll-migration

Review feedback logged:
- 2026-03-10 (Design): request to include one-click "request migration support" button in console (accepted).
- 2026-03-11 (Security): confirm there are no new data exposure vectors from the migration wrapper (security review completed, no issues).

Post-shutdown steps:
- Remove longpoll code paths from runtime after 90 days of shutdown, behind an archival branch.
- Final documentation update and archive deprecation notices.
